title: Liberty
notes: This chunk is dense, law-positive, and symbolically tight: jubilee as the sole biblical liberty, the swallow nesting at the altar, the bored ear at the doorpost, and the Jeremiah symmetry all land with force. Verse assembly is clean and the modern counterfeit is named without hedging. Residual defects are house-style only—multiple author sentences open with And, plus presenter staging (Notice, mark). No AI stock vocabulary, no broken math or mistyped quotes, and no doctrine rewrites required. Surgical openers and cue removals will restore the book’s assertive register without thinning density.

proposals.old:
Notice what kind of thing this liberty is.
It is not the absence of law; it is a command _of_ the law.
proposals.new: This liberty is not the absence of law; it is a command _of_ the law.
proposals.summary: Remove director cue and merge into a direct assertion.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Notice-that staging. The claim stands stronger as a plain assertion without the cue.

proposals.old: And the jubilee is the crown of a rhythm the law keeps beating: every seventh year is a release — debts let go, the Hebrew servant sent out free (Deuteronomy 15:1-2; Exodus 21:2) — seven sevens of years, and then the trumpet of the fiftieth.
proposals.new: The jubilee is the crown of a rhythm the law keeps beating: every seventh year is a release — debts let go, the Hebrew servant sent out free (Deuteronomy 15:1-2; Exodus 21:2) — seven sevens of years, and then the trumpet of the fiftieth.
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: Author sentences may not open with And. Removing it keeps the claim intact and meets house style.

proposals.old: And this is the passage Jesus stood up and read in the synagogue at Nazareth, closing the book with __“this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears”__ (Luke 4:21) — a release year, for He proclaimed the release in the year the law appoints it.
proposals.new: This is the passage Jesus stood up and read in the synagogue at Nazareth, closing the book with __“this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears”__ (Luke 4:21) — a release year, for He proclaimed the release in the year the law appoints it.
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: Author sentences may not open with And. The historical claim needs no conjunction opener.

proposals.old: And where does Scripture set the free bird’s nest?
proposals.new: Where does Scripture set the free bird’s nest?
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: Author sentences may not open with And. The rhetorical question stands cleanly without it.

proposals.new: The instrument of release is stated in the same breath: the sym:sym-truth[truth]footnote:truthlaw[_Truth_ — God’s law, __“thy law is the truth”__ (Psalm 119:142); established in the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/the-way-the-truth-and-the-life/[The Way, the Truth & the Life].] — which Scripture defines as God’s law — is what makes free.
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: Author sentences may not open with And. Markup and footnote are preserved exactly.

proposals.old: Offered the open sky, the servant chooses the house — for sym:sym-love[love], which Scripture defines as keeping the master’s commandments — and mark where and how the choice is sealed: his *ear*, at the *door post*.
proposals.new: Offered the open sky, the servant chooses the house — for sym:sym-love[love], which Scripture defines as keeping the master’s commandments — and the choice is sealed at his *ear*, at the *door post*.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids Mark-that staging. The seal location remains the same claim without the cue.

proposals.old: And Jesus set the two figures side by side in the same breath as His teaching on freedom: __“the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the *Son abideth ever*”__ (John 8:35) — the Son is the one who stays in the Father’s house by nature, and the freed slave who loves his Master stays by choice.
proposals.new: Jesus set the two figures side by side in the same breath as His teaching on freedom: __“the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the *Son abideth ever*”__ (John 8:35) — the Son is the one who stays in the Father’s house by nature, and the freed slave who loves his Master stays by choice.
proposals.summary: Drop leading And from author prose.
proposals.rationale: Author sentences may not open with And. The Son/servant pairing claim is unchanged.

proposals.old: And whether a man, once freed, will hear and serve is the whole difference between the sym:sym-fool[fool] and the sym:sym-wise[wise] — the next chapter.
proposals.new: Whether a man, once freed, will hear and serve is the whole difference between the sym:sym-fool[fool] and the sym:sym-wise[wise] — the next chapter.
